title: Moment of Inertia
short_intro: The moment of inertia is a quantitative measure of a rigid body's rotational inertia, representing its resistance to angular acceleration about a rotational axis. It depends on both the mass distribution relative to the axis of rotation and the chosen axis itself.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Calculation of moment of inertia for standard symmetrical bodies (ring, disc, rod, sphere, cylinder) using parallel and perpendicular axes theorems, and elementary problems on rotational kinetic energy.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: General tensor formulation of inertia, principal moments of inertia, products of inertia, complex composite body integrations, and non-inertial frame rotational dynamics.

prerequisites: Newton's laws of motion for rotational systems
Centre of mass definition and coordinate calculation
Calculus integration techniques for continuous mass distribution

concept_notes.heading: Definition and Physical Significance
bullets: Mathematically defined as I = sum(m_i r_i^2) for discrete systems and I = integral(r^2 dm) for continuous systems.
Acts as the rotational analogue of mass in linear translational motion.
Has SI units of kg m^2 and dimensional formula [ML^2].

concept_notes.heading: Theorem of Perpendicular Axes
bullets: Applicable strictly to plane laminar (two-dimensional) bodies.

States that the moment of inertia about an axis perpendicular to the plane (I_z) equals the sum of moments of inertia about two mutually perpendicular axes in the plane meeting at the origin (I_x + I_y).
Expressed mathematically as I_z = I_x + I_y.

concept_notes.heading: Theorem of Parallel Axes
bullets: Applicable to any rigid body of any shape (1D, 2D, or 3D).

States that the moment of inertia about any axis is equal to the moment of inertia about a parallel axis passing through the centre of mass plus the product of total mass and the square of the perpendicular distance between the axes.
Expressed mathematically as I = I_cm + Md^2.

concept_notes.heading: Radius of Gyration
bullets: Defined as the root-mean-square distance of the constituent particles from the axis of rotation.
Expressed as k = sqrt(I / M), where M is total mass and I is moment of inertia.
Represents the geometric distribution of mass relative to the axis.

derivations.title: Moment of Inertia of a Uniform Thin Rod
derivations.conditions: Axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its length, length L, mass M.
steps: Consider a uniform thin rod of mass M and length L aligned along the x-axis from x = -L/2 to x = L/2.
Define linear mass density lambda = M/L. Consider a small mass element dm = lambda dx = (M/L) dx at a distance x from the centre.
Integrate the differential moment of inertia dI = x^2 dm from -L/2 to L/2.

derivations.title: Moment of Inertia of a Uniform Circular Ring
derivations.conditions: Axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane, radius R, mass M.
steps: Consider a thin circular ring of total mass M and radius R.
Since all mass elements of the ring are situated at the same perpendicular distance R from the axis passing through the centre perpendicular to the plane:
Write the definition of moment of inertia I = integral r^2 dm.
Substitute r = R to get I = R^2 integral dm.

formula_sheet.name: General Discrete System
formula_sheet.variables: m_i = mass of particle i, r_i = perpendicular distance from axis

formula_sheet.name: General Continuous System
formula_sheet.variables: dm = differential mass element, r = perpendicular distance

formula_sheet.name: Perpendicular Axes Theorem
formula_sheet.variables: I_x, I_y = axes in plane; I_z = axis perpendicular to plane

formula_sheet.name: Parallel Axes Theorem
formula_sheet.variables: I_cm = moment of inertia about centre of mass, d = distance between parallel axes

graphs_and_experiments.title: Torsional Pendulum Experiment
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Graph of time period squared (T^2) versus moment of inertia (I) of added standard masses.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: A straight line passing through the origin or intercepting the axis confirming T = 2pisqrt{I/C}, allowing determination of torsional constant C.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Directly tested in experimental physics viva and conceptual numericals on torsional oscillations.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Radius of Gyration Dependence on Axis Position
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Plot of moment of inertia I versus squared distance x^2 from centre of mass using parallel axis theorem.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Linear graph with slope equal to total mass M and intercept equal to I_cm.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Used to evaluate graphical problems based on the parallel axes theorem.

solved_numericals.question: Find the moment of inertia of a uniform circular disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane.
solution_steps: Identify the formula for the moment of inertia of a disc about its central transverse axis: I = (1/2) M R^2.
Substitute the given values: M = 2 kg, R = 0.5 m.

solved_numericals.question: Calculate the moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod of mass 1.2 kg and length 1 m about an axis passing through one of its ends and perpendicular to its length.
solution_steps: Use the parallel axis theorem or direct integration for an axis at the end: I = (1/3) M L^2.
Substitute M = 1.2 kg and L = 1 m.

solved_numericals.question: A uniform circular disc has mass M and radius R. Find its moment of inertia about an axis tangent to its edge and lying in the plane of the disc.
solution_steps: First, find the moment of inertia of the disc about a diametrical axis in its plane: I_diam = (1/4) M R^2.
Apply the parallel axes theorem between the diametrical axis and the tangent axis in the plane, where the separation distance is d = R.
Calculate: I_tangent = I_diam + M R^2 = (1/4) M R^2 + M R^2 = (5/4) M R^2.

assumptions_and_limitations: The body is treated as rigid, meaning distances between constituent particles remain invariant under applied forces and torques.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Moment of inertia is a constant intrinsic property of a body like mass.
common_misconceptions.correct: Moment of inertia depends on the choice of the axis of rotation.
common_misconceptions.why: Mass is scalar and independent of position, whereas r in mr^2 is measured perpendicularly from a specific rotational axis.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Perpendicular axes theorem can be applied to any three-dimensional solid object.
common_misconceptions.correct: The theorem is strictly valid only for two-dimensional planar laminar bodies.
common_misconceptions.why: For 3D bodies, I_z = I_x + I_y does not hold because z-coordinates of mass elements are non-zero.

quick_revision: Moment of inertia (I = sum m_i r_i^2) measures rotational inertia and depends heavily on the axis of rotation.
General Discrete System: I = sum_{i=1}^{n} m_i r_i^2
General Continuous System: I = int r^2 dm
